note: Quick, Draw! hourglass 5880797120692224 from the Czech Republic, four strokes: stroke 0 is the top plate, a long flat closed loop; stroke 1 is the left side of the glass, pinched in at the waist; stroke 2 is the right side of the glass, drawn bottom to top, pinched at the waist; stroke 3 is the base plate, a single line with a small tail at its left end. The hourglass is a rigid object, so the whole doodle is placed by two points, the centre of the top plate and the centre of the base plate. Their direction turns the drawing with the hourglass as the hand tips it upright. When the hourglass points toward the camera the distance between the two points shortens and the drawing shortens along its axis while keeping its width, which is how a turn toward the viewer reads in a flat drawing. Nothing else in the hourglass moves; the hand that turns it is not drawn.
